title: Fair-value gap candidate outcome study
status: screening research, not arbitrage and not a trade recommendation

method.signal: First completed hourly option trade bar each day; one row per unique contract.
method.forecast: hv20, selected only on the first eight expirations by variance MSE; last four expirations held out.
method.fairValue: American CRR tree (75 steps) using the forecast-volatility level while preserving the same-day market smile.
method.entry: Next hour's first trade; a candidate is not entered if the model gap no longer exceeds the cost haircut.
method.target: Original signal-time model fair value, held fixed for the target test.
method.conservativeExit: Target counted only when a later hourly closing trade reaches it; otherwise the last observed trade is used.
method.optimisticExit: Target counted when a later hourly high touches it; this is an upper bound, not proof of an executable fill.
method.costs: 10% of entry premium with a $0.05 minimum round-trip haircut.

caveats: The historical source contains trades, not NBBO bid/ask quotes or depth. Entry and exit prices can be stale and are not guaranteed fills.
Only 22 contracts are available per day, so this pilot cannot honestly select 50 contracts per day.
Coverage is SPY and 0–4 DTE only. Rows for 5–10 DTE are deliberately marked unavailable.
A model gap is not arbitrage. Forecast error, smile dynamics, theta, jumps, liquidity, assignment, fees, and execution can erase it.
Calibration-period charts are diagnostic. Performance claims should use the untouched holdout only.
